title: approvals: GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id/actions answers 200 {"data":[]} for an unknown request id, where GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id answers 404
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcV2ijbfB8Drvs2oik6

QA-source: #27481 · approvals.account-app-entry · observed beside the clauses

Found by an off-clause probe in the 18.3.0 release-candidate QA run (wave anchor #27377, card W3-C1), subject `c4c515ad`, stock showcase boot.

## Reproduction
1. As any signed-in user (the seeded admin, or a non-admin approver persona), `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/areq_does-not-exist` → 404.
2. `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/areq_does-not-exist/actions` → **200 `{"data":[]}`**.
3. For a request the persona cannot see, the same pair answers 404 and 200 `{"data":[]}`. The admin's read of that request's actions lists its `submit` row.

Expected: the sub-resource answers an unknown parent the way the parent does (404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`), so a client can tell "no actions yet" from "no such request". Actual: an empty 200, which reads as "this request exists and has no actions".

No existence information leaks: an unknown id and an invisible id answer the same, which is correct. Only the unknown-parent answer is wrong.

## Mechanism
`packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts`, the `GET …/approvals/requests/:id/actions` handler (around line 576), calls `svc.listActions(req.params.id, context)` and answers `res.json({ data: rows })`. It never resolves the parent request first, so an unknown id is an empty list rather than the 404 the sibling `GET …/requests/:id` handler answers. This is the same class as #25486 (doors that answer an unknown resource as empty where their siblings answer 404), on a door that card did not cover.

## Severity
Low: an API consistency defect.

Dedupe: searched open and closed issues for "approvals actions unknown id 200 empty". The class card #25486 is closed and did not cover this route.
